_meta.indication: Treatment of intermediate or high-risk myelofibrosis (MF), including primary MF or secondary MF (post-PV and post-ET), in adults with anemia.

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, danazol (DAN)-controlled superiority trial; subjects randomized 2:1 to momelotinib or danazol.
pivotal_trials.population: Symptomatic, anemic adults with intermediate or high-risk MF previously treated with an approved JAK inhibitor.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: MFSAF v4.0 TSS response rate at Week 24 (proportion with ≥50% reduction in mean TSS vs baseline).
pivotal_trials.result: MFSAF v4.0 TSS response rate 24.6% (MMB) vs 9.2% (DAN); treatment difference 15.7% (95% CI 5.5%, 25.8%); 2-sided p=0.0095.

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, active-controlled (ruxolitinib) noninferiority trial; subjects randomized 1:1 to momelotinib 200 mg once daily or ruxolitinib.
pivotal_trials.population: JAK inhibitor-naive adults with primary MF, post-PV MF, or post-ET MF.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Splenic response rate (SRR) at Week 24 (noninferiority of MMB vs RUX in spleen volume reduction).
pivotal_trials.result: Met primary endpoint (noninferiority): SRR at Week 24 26.5% (MMB) vs 29.5% (RUX); noninferiority treatment difference 9% (95% CI 2%, 16%); 2-sided p=0.014. The key secondary TSS noninferiority endpoint was NOT met.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥20%) are thrombocytopenia, hemorrhage, bacterial infection, fatigue, dizziness, diarrhea, and nausea. In MOMENTUM, thrombocytopenia occurred in 28% (Grade ≥3 22%) with MMB vs 17% (12%) with danazol; serious adverse reactions in 35% and fatal adverse reactions in 12% (most commonly viral infection 5%).
target_moa: Oral small-molecule inhibitor of wild-type JAK1 and JAK2; also inhibits activin A receptor type 1 (ACVR1/ALK2), inhibiting liver hepcidin expression and increasing iron availability to improve red blood cell production.

advisory_committee.vote: No Advisory Committee meeting was convened; the application did not raise efficacy or safety issues requiring external expert advice.

basis.text: Breakthrough therapy designation was requested but withdrawn by the applicant (Sierra) on February 6, 2019.

summary.text: OJJAARA (momelotinib) received a standard review under the 505(b)(1) pathway with Orphan drug designation (granted August 5, 2010) and Fast Track designation (granted May 31, 2019); a breakthrough therapy request was withdrawn in 2019. It was approved on full (traditional) approval based on the MOMENTUM and SIMPLIFY-1 trials, without an Advisory Committee meeting.

citations.quote: The Applicant, GlaxoSmithKline LLC, seeks approval of momelotinib (MMB), under the 505(b)(1) regulatory pathway, for the treatment of intermediate or high-risk MF, including primary MF or secondary MF (post-PV and post-ET), in adults with anemia.
MMB was granted an Orphan drug designation on August 5, 2010, and Fast Track designation on May 31, 2019.
This application did not raise efficacy or safety issues requiring external expert advice. Therefore, an Advisory Committee meeting was not convened to discuss this application.
